questions.explanation: Loans supplement revenue for projects such as railways and power plants whose benefits last many years.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Fiscal policy refers to the use of
questions.A: taxation and government expenditure to influence the economy
questions.B: interest rates and the money supply to influence the economy
questions.C: tariffs alone to protect industries
questions.D: exchange controls to manage the currency
questions.explanation: Fiscal policy is the budget side; monetary policy is the central bank's domain.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: The removal of the petrol subsidy in Nigeria in 2023 was expected mainly to
questions.A: reduce government expenditure and free funds for other uses
questions.B: lower the pump price of petrol
questions.C: increase the government's spending on subsidies
questions.D: reduce the revenue of state governments
questions.explanation: Subsidy payments had consumed a large share of revenue; removal was meant to save funds, though it raised petrol prices.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A supplementary budget is
questions.A: additional spending approved after the main budget proves insufficient
questions.B: the annual budget presented by a state government to its assembly
questions.C: a budget in which planned revenue is exactly equal to planned spending
questions.D: a budget prepared by the central bank for its own annual operations
questions.explanation: Supplementary appropriations cover unforeseen expenditure during the financial year.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A government's revenue is ₦12 trillion and its expenditure is ₦16 trillion, of which ₦5 trillion is debt service. Its fiscal deficit is
questions.A: ₦4 trillion
questions.B: ₦9 trillion
questions.C: ₦1 trillion
questions.D: ₦5 trillion
questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit = expenditure − revenue = 16 − 12 = ₦4 trillion.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A tax whose burden cannot be shifted to another person is
questions.A: a direct tax
questions.B: an indirect tax
questions.C: a regressive tax
questions.D: an excise duty
questions.explanation: Personal income tax and company tax are borne by the person or firm on whom they are levied.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Value added tax (VAT) is classified as
questions.A: an indirect tax
questions.B: a direct tax
questions.C: a progressive tax
questions.D: a capital tax
questions.explanation: VAT is levied on goods and services and its burden is passed on to the final consumer in the price.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Nigeria's VAT rate of 7.5% is charged on most goods. If a consumer pays ₦21,500 for a product including VAT, the price before VAT was

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Under a progressive tax system, a person earning ₦1 million pays ₦50,000 in tax. A person earning ₦5 million would pay
questions.A: more than ₦250,000
questions.B: exactly ₦250,000
questions.C: less than ₦250,000
questions.D: exactly ₦50,000
questions.explanation: Progressive taxation takes a larger percentage as income rises; 5% of ₦5 million is ₦250,000, so a higher rate means more than that.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A flat tax of ₦500 per person, levied on rich and poor alike, is
questions.A: regressive, because it takes a larger share of a poor person's income
questions.B: progressive, because the rich pay the same amount
questions.C: proportional, because everyone pays the same amount
questions.D: a direct tax that cannot be regressive
questions.explanation: The same sum is a bigger percentage of a small income than of a large one.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A tax that takes the same percentage of income from everybody is
questions.A: proportional
questions.B: progressive
questions.C: regressive
questions.D: indirect
questions.explanation: Under a proportional tax the rate is constant whatever the income.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: The canon of taxation that requires the cost of collecting a tax to be small relative to the revenue it yields is
questions.A: economy
questions.B: certainty
questions.C: convenience
questions.D: equity
questions.explanation: Adam Smith's canons are equity, certainty, convenience and economy.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE), under which tax is deducted from salaries monthly, satisfies mainly the canon of
questions.A: convenience
questions.B: economy
questions.C: equity
questions.D: flexibility
questions.explanation: Tax is collected at the time and in the manner most convenient for the taxpayer.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A tax on cigarette manufacturers is passed on to smokers through higher prices. Economists say that the ______ of the tax has shifted to the smokers.
questions.A: incidence (final burden)
questions.B: rate of collection
questions.C: collecting agency
questions.D: purpose of spending
questions.explanation: Formal incidence is on the person who pays the government; effective incidence is on whoever ultimately bears it.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A tax of ₦100 per unit is placed on a good whose demand is perfectly inelastic. The burden of the tax falls
questions.A: entirely on consumers
questions.B: entirely on producers
questions.C: equally on consumers and producers
questions.D: on the government
questions.explanation: With perfectly inelastic demand consumers buy the same quantity at any price, so the whole tax is passed on to them.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of indirect taxes?
questions.A: they are difficult to evade because they are included in prices
questions.B: they fall more heavily on the rich than on the poor
questions.C: their burden is always borne by producers
questions.D: they do not affect the prices of goods
questions.explanation: Everyone who buys taxed goods pays; but they tend to be regressive.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: The body responsible for collecting company income tax and VAT in Nigeria is the
questions.A: Federal Inland Revenue Service
questions.B: Central Bank of Nigeria
questions.C: Nigeria Customs Service
questions.D: Bureau of Public Enterprises
questions.explanation: FIRS administers federal taxes; states collect personal income tax through their internal revenue services.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A tax on the profits of companies is
questions.A: a direct tax
questions.B: an indirect tax
questions.C: a customs duty
questions.D: an excise duty
questions.explanation: Company income tax is levied directly on the firm's profits and cannot easily be shifted.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Governments impose taxes for all of the following reasons EXCEPT to
questions.A: increase the consumption of harmful goods
questions.B: raise revenue for public services
questions.C: redistribute income from rich to poor
questions.D: protect infant industries from imports
questions.explanation: Taxes on alcohol and tobacco aim to reduce, not increase, their consumption.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Mr Adeyemi earns ₦3 million a year. The first ₦300,000 is tax-free, the next ₦300,000 is taxed at 7% and the rest at 15%. His tax is

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Economic growth differs from economic development in that growth refers to
questions.A: an increase in a country's total output, while development includes welfare
questions.B: improvements in health and education, while development means more output
questions.C: the fair distribution of income, while development means higher exports
questions.D: the change from agriculture to industry, while development means more trade
questions.explanation: Growth is a rise in real output; development also involves structural change and better living standards.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: The Human Development Index measures a country's development using
questions.A: life expectancy, education and income per head
questions.B: the size of its army and population
questions.C: its total exports and imports
questions.D: the number of cars per household
questions.explanation: The HDI combines health, knowledge and standard of living into one index.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of a developing country?
questions.A: a large proportion of the labour force in agriculture
questions.B: a very high income per head
questions.C: a low birth rate and an ageing population
questions.D: a highly developed manufacturing sector
questions.explanation: Developing economies typically depend heavily on primary production and have low productivity.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: The vicious circle of poverty describes a situation in which
questions.A: low income leads to low savings, low investment and hence low income again
questions.B: rich countries grow richer every year while poor countries grow poorer
questions.C: poor countries cannot borrow from abroad because they have no collateral
questions.D: population falls as income rises, so the labour force keeps shrinking
questions.explanation: Low incomes prevent the saving needed for investment, so productivity and incomes stay low.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Foreign aid can help a developing country's development mainly by
questions.A: supplementing domestic savings to finance investment
questions.B: increasing the country's dependency on imports permanently
questions.C: reducing the level of education
questions.D: replacing the need for domestic taxation
questions.explanation: Aid can fill the gap between the investment needed and the savings available, if well used.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A serious obstacle to economic development in Nigeria is
questions.A: corruption and poor infrastructure
questions.B: an excess of skilled manpower
questions.C: too much capital investment
questions.D: an ageing population
questions.explanation: Diversion of public funds and unreliable power and transport raise costs and discourage investment.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Nigeria's economy is described as under-developed rather than undeveloped because
questions.A: it has large resources that are not yet fully and efficiently used
questions.B: it has no natural resources at all and must import all its raw materials
questions.C: its population is too small to provide the labour needed for development
questions.D: it has already reached its full potential and cannot develop any further
questions.explanation: Under-development implies unexploited potential in land, minerals and people.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Which of the following is an indicator of improved economic development?
questions.A: a rise in life expectancy and literacy rates
questions.B: a rise in the number of people below the poverty line
questions.C: an increase in infant mortality
questions.D: a rise in the share of agriculture in employment
questions.explanation: Development shows in better health, education and living standards, not just in output figures.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) adopted by the United Nations in 2015 aim, among other things, to
questions.A: end poverty and hunger and ensure quality education and health by 2030
questions.B: increase military spending in poor countries to guarantee their security
questions.C: abolish international trade between developed and developing countries
questions.D: reduce the population of the world by half before the end of the century
questions.explanation: The 17 SDGs cover poverty, hunger, health, education, gender equality, clean energy and climate action.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Economic diversification is recommended for Nigeria mainly to
questions.A: reduce dependence on crude oil for revenue and foreign exchange
questions.B: increase the share of oil in total exports
questions.C: reduce the output of the agricultural sector
questions.D: discourage the growth of small businesses
questions.explanation: A broader base of exports and revenue makes the economy less vulnerable to oil price shocks.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Human capital development refers to
questions.A: investment in education, training and health to raise the productivity of people
questions.B: the building of factories, roads, bridges and railways by the government
questions.C: the accumulation of foreign reserves by the central bank of a country
questions.D: the purchase of modern machinery and equipment from foreign countries
questions.explanation: Healthier, better-educated workers are more productive and adaptable.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A country's real GDP grew by 3% in a year in which its population grew by 3.5%. Its real income per head
questions.A: fell slightly
questions.B: rose slightly
questions.C: was unchanged
questions.D: doubled
questions.explanation: When population grows faster than output, output per person falls.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Economic planning is
questions.A: the deliberate direction of a country's resources towards chosen objectives
questions.B: the annual budget speech delivered by the minister of finance
questions.C: the recording of the economic transactions of the past financial year
questions.D: the fixing of the prices of goods and services by private business firms
questions.explanation: Plans set targets for growth, employment and infrastructure and outline the means of achieving them.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Nigeria's First National Development Plan covered the period
questions.explanation: The First Plan was launched in 1962; the Second (1970–74) followed the civil war.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A plan that lays down targets for each sector of the economy and directs resources to meet them is
questions.A: a comprehensive (central) plan
questions.B: an indicative plan
questions.C: a rolling plan
questions.D: a perspective plan
questions.explanation: Comprehensive plans are typical of centrally planned economies; indicative plans only guide private decisions.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Nigeria's 1990–1992 plan was reviewed at the end of 1990 and extended to cover 1991–1993, and this was repeated every year. Such a plan is described as
questions.A: a rolling plan
questions.B: a fixed five-year plan
questions.C: a local government plan
questions.D: a twenty-year perspective plan
questions.explanation: Nigeria adopted three-year rolling plans in 1990 to allow adjustment to changing conditions.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A perspective plan differs from a medium-term plan in that it
questions.A: sets broad goals for a long period such as 15 to 25 years
questions.B: covers only one financial year and is revised every month
questions.C: is prepared by private firms rather than by the government
questions.D: contains no targets at all, only a description of the economy
questions.explanation: Nigeria's Vision 2010 and Vision 20:2020 were long-term perspective plans.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A common reason for the failure of development plans in Nigeria is
questions.A: inadequate and unreliable statistical data
questions.B: the absence of any natural resources
questions.C: too much money in the treasury
questions.D: the very small size of the population
questions.explanation: Poor data on population, output and prices make targets unrealistic; political instability and corruption also contribute.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Which of the following is an objective of economic planning?
questions.A: raising the standard of living and reducing unemployment
questions.B: increasing the rate of inflation
questions.C: widening the gap between rich and poor
questions.D: reducing the output of the economy
questions.explanation: Plans aim at growth, employment, price stability, balanced regional development and fairer income distribution.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Nigeria's Structural Adjustment Programme (SAP) of 1986 was introduced mainly to
questions.A: restructure the economy by reducing dependence on oil and liberalising markets
questions.B: nationalise all the foreign companies operating in the country's oil sector
questions.C: increase the number of commodity marketing boards buying farmers' produce
questions.D: fix the exchange rate of the naira permanently at one naira to one dollar
questions.explanation: SAP devalued the naira, abolished marketing boards, privatised enterprises and removed many controls.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: In an indicative plan, the government
questions.A: sets out expected trends and encourages private firms to follow them
questions.B: directly owns and runs all the industries and farms in the country
questions.C: forbids private individuals and firms from investing in the economy
questions.D: fixes the prices of all goods and services sold in the country
questions.explanation: Indicative planning guides rather than commands, using incentives to steer the private sector.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Adequate funding, reliable data and political stability are
questions.A: conditions for successful economic planning
questions.B: obstacles to economic planning
questions.C: features of a subsistence economy
questions.D: canons of taxation
questions.explanation: Without finance, information and continuity of policy, plan targets are unlikely to be met.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Nigeria's National Development Plan 2021–2025 emphasised
questions.A: diversification, infrastructure and job creation
questions.B: a return to marketing boards
questions.C: the abolition of private enterprise
questions.D: the reduction of the labour force
questions.explanation: Recent plans have focused on growing non-oil sectors, closing infrastructure gaps and creating jobs for the youth.
